title: Apex managed sharing across a record lifecycle
summary: Maintain a manager's record access while preserving unrelated grants and handling bulk changes.
prerequisites: Bulk-safe Apex, maps, sets, triggers, and assertions.
learningObjectives: Use a custom RowCause to identify owned shares.
Handle manager changes, clearing, and restoration.
Preserve independent access and test 200 records.

sections.heading: Understand the mechanism
body: Some access requirements follow business data rather than the role hierarchy. Northstar appoints a manager to an internal project, and that manager needs Read while assigned. A sharing rule based only on fixed groups may not express this relationship. Apex managed sharing lets application logic maintain the specific record-level grant.

Create Project__c as a separate custom object with a Text Name, private organization-wide defaults, and Manager__c as a lookup to User. These fields are not in the starter. Add an Apex Sharing Reason named Assigned_Manager. Its API value becomes Assigned_Manager__c in the share record's RowCause. RowCause is the reason for the grant; it lets your process distinguish its work from Manual, Owner, or another application's reason.

Treat processing as reconciliation: calculate the desired manager grants, compare them with existing shares for your reason, then insert missing grants and remove obsolete ones. For a change from Anna to Oleg, delete only Anna's Assigned_Manager grant and add Oleg's grant. Anna may retain access through another path. That is not necessarily a defect in your handler.

Current metadata supports sharing reasons for eligible standard objects from API 68.0, so the old statement 'custom reasons are always custom-object-only' is no longer universally correct. This exercise deliberately uses Project__c for a clear owned schema. Check eligibility before extending the pattern to a standard object. Also define the privileged execution boundary: creating shares must not become an unrestricted public endpoint.

callouts.text: Your handler owns one reason for sharing, not every possible reason a person can see the record.

sections.heading: Northstar Motors worked example
body: Project P-1 starts with Manager=Anna. After processing, Anna has an Assigned_Manager Read grant. Oleg also has an independent Manual grant. When Manager changes to Oleg, remove only the old custom-reason grant and create or reconcile Oleg's custom-reason grant. The Manual grant remains. Clearing Manager removes your custom-reason grant, while independent access can remain.

The following fragment shows the shape of one share; it is not a complete trigger or deployable service. Reconciliation, bulk collection, error handling, authorization, and lifecycle dispatch still have to be implemented. Do not copy a one-row demonstration into a loop containing DML.

callouts.text: If Anna keeps a Manual share after being replaced, should your handler delete it?

sections.heading: Build and inspect
body: Create Project__c, Manager__c, and the sharing reason first. Give test personas object Read and necessary FLS separately. Record API versions and the explicit security mode used by the privileged sharing operation.

steps.title: Specify transitions
steps.instruction: Write expected custom-reason grants for insert, same-manager update, A→B, A→null, null→A, delete/undelete, and owner change.
steps.expected: Each transition defines your own grant independently of total visibility.

steps.title: Implement reconciliation
steps.instruction: Query shares only for relevant project IDs and your RowCause. Collect inserts and deletes outside loops. Define behavior for an inactive manager and a manager who is also owner.
steps.expected: Repeated processing produces no unnecessary duplicates or unrelated deletions.

steps.title: Verify lifecycle and bulk
steps.instruction: Run assertions over 200 projects and the transition table. Include an independent Manual grant and inspect it after manager replacement.
steps.expected: The independent grant survives and all intended custom grants match the final data.

sections.heading: Failure cases and boundaries
body: Deleting all Project__Share rows for the previous manager destroys unrelated access. A broad query can make a superficially passing test conceal this defect.

Delete and undelete require explicit reasoning about restored data and shares. Do not claim they work because update tests pass. Define whether restoration reconciles immediately and prove the chosen behavior.

callouts.text: A sharing service must have an authorized entry point; do not expose arbitrary parent IDs and user IDs to unrestricted callers.

exercise.title: Maintain assigned-manager access
exercise.brief: Implement the transition table on Project__c and submit evidence of safe reconciliation.
steps: Implement and test only your RowCause.
acceptance: Cleared and changed managers remove the obsolete owned grant.
Bulk and undelete behavior are explicitly tested.
exercise.stretch: Explain one limitation and propose a small follow-up experiment before extending the implementation.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why use a custom reason?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It identifies the process-owned grant and supports the intended managed-sharing lifecycle.

knowledgeCheck.question: Does removing the old grant guarantee denial?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Independent access may still exist and must be assessed separately.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is insert-only logic insufficient?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Assignments change, clear, and may be restored after deletion; stale grants otherwise persist.

recap: Test every lifecycle transition and authorization boundary.
